summary: Practise produce inspection, cold-chain monitoring, HACCP controls, and traceability. Explore this five-day postharvest quality course.
lede: Postharvest quality control training helps fresh-produce teams assess and protect product condition from harvest through storage and dispatch. For supervisors, inspectors and quality staff, it develops practical skills in maturity and defect checks, cold-chain monitoring, lot traceability and corrective-action records. Learners use inspection and temperature data to identify issues, document decisions and plan follow-up across packhouse and distribution operations.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is for professionals who make or verify fresh-produce handling decisions, maintain quality records, and coordinate responses to postharvest defects across the supply chain. This course is designed for: Postharvest quality inspectors who grade produce and record defects at receiving. Packhouse supervisors who coordinate washing, sorting, packing, and dispatch checks. Produce quality assurance officers who verify specifications and corrective-action records. Cold-chain coordinators who monitor storage temperatures and escalate excursions. Harvest supervisors who assess maturity and coordinate careful field handling. Fresh-produce storage managers who control humidity, ventilation, and stock rotation. Food safety officers who connect HACCP controls with postharvest hygiene procedures. Agricultural extension specialists who advise growers on handling and quality practices. Produce procurement officers who assess supplier quality records and incoming lots. Supply-chain traceability coordinators who maintain lot identification and product movement records.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of fresh-produce handling, packing, storage, or food-quality procedures is expected. No coding is required. Spreadsheet familiarity is useful for the digital quality-log exercise.
